title: Unwinding Anxiety: New Science Shows How to Break the Cycles of Worry and Fear to Heal You
description: New York Times and Wall Street Journal bestseller A step-by-step plan clinically proven to break the cycle of worry and fear that drives anxiety and addictive habits We are living through one of the most anxious periods any of us can remember. Whether facing issues as public as a pandemic or as personal as having kids at home and fighting the urge to reach for the wine bottle every night, we are feeling overwhelmed and out of control. But in this timely book, Judson Brewer explains how to uproot anxiety at its source using brain-based techniques and small hacks accessible to anyone. We think of anxiety as everything from mild unease to full-blown panic. But it's also what drives the addictive behaviors and bad habits we use to cope (e.g. stress eating, procrastination, doom scrolling and social media). Plus, anxiety lives in a part of the brain that resists rational thought. So we get stuck in anxiety habit loops that we can't think our way out of or use willpower to overcome. Dr. Brewer teaches us to map our brains to discover our triggers, defuse them with the simple but powerful practice of curiosity, and to train our brains using mindfulness and other practices that his lab has proven can work. title: Overthinking and Anxiety Relief: A Practical Guide for Women to Calm Anxiety and Take Back
description: If you’ve ever lain awake at 3 a.m. running a mental board meeting while everyone else sleeps, you’re not broken, and you’re not alone. When your mind replays conversations, overanalyzes decisions, and refuses to “switch off,” it can leave you feeling mentally exhausted, emotionally drained, and frustrated with yourself for not being able to relax. Overthinking and Anxiety Relief is a practical, compassionate guide for women who feel stuck in cycles of worry, overthinking, and self-doubt. If your brain feels like a browser with dozens of tabs open, this book was written for you. Inside, you’ll discover how to: Recognize the mental patterns that keep you trapped in overthinking Interrupt obsessive thought spirals before they take over your day Make decisions without replaying them for hours or days afterward Stop mistaking anxiety-driven thinking for control or productivity Calm your nervous system in ways that go beyond willpower Feel clearer, steadier, and more emotionally grounded Each chapter follows simple and practical tools you can apply immediately, without complicated routines or years of therapy. title: Anxiety Relief: Self Help (With Heart) For Anxiety, Panic Attacks, And Stress Management
description: Is stress, anxiety, or panic ruining your life? Are you tired of failing to recover? Are those "quick fix" approaches failing to deliver results? That may well be because you're much more like a garden than you are an electrical appliance. Healing anxiety is an organic process, not just nuts and bolts. Anxiety Specialist Therapist, John Crawford, learned this the hard way when he experienced a terrifying descent into severe anxiety and depression during his twenties and spent many fruitless years seeking the elusive "quick fix" solution before finally meeting a gifted therapist who guided him skilfully to understand what makes a full recovery possible. Now, almost 25 years later, with that understanding fully cemented, John has spent the last 13 years of his life working as a professional therapist, specialising in the treatment of anxiety disorders. Anxiety Relief is a warm, compassionate, and expert book to help anxious, panicky, or stressed people, written from both sides of the therapeutic couch. If you're suffering, and you don't know how to gain relief from your anxiety, then this book is for you. It's wide in scope but laser-focused on ensuring that you get results. The tools and understanding presented here are the same proven tools that John has been using to help anxious people recover for many years. Inside "Anxiety Relief" you’ll discover:- How to create the correct mindset for full and permanent recovery from (even severe) anxiety. How to fully understand the brain’s evolutionary role in creating stress, anxiety, depression, panic and negative thinking, and how to use that understanding to take back control. title: The Polyvagal Healing Workbook: The Practical Guide to Regulate Your Nervous System, Heal
description: The Polyvagal Healing Workbook: The Practical Guide to Regulate Your Nervous System, Heal Trauma Safely, and Find Relief from Anxiety and Chronic Stress is a compassionate, science-based roadmap for restoring calm, safety, and resilience. Drawing from the pioneering work of Stephen Porges, Deb Dana, Peter Levine, and Bessel van der Kolk, this workbook helps readers gently heal trauma without retraumatization. It explores how the autonomic nervous system, vagus nerve, and mind-body connection influence emotional balance, chronic stress management, and long-term recovery. With practical guidance rooted in polyvagal theory and somatic therapy, it offers tools for nervous system regulation, mindfulness, and trauma release that bring safety back into the body and mind. Polyvagal Theory Understand how neuroception, the window of tolerance, and the autonomic nervous system shape your sense of safety, connection, and emotional regulation. Vagus Nerve Tools Learn how to use vagus nerve stimulation, breathwork, and mindful movement to improve vagal tone, ease anxiety, and support self-regulation techniques. Somatic Therapy Explore grounding techniques, somatic exercises, and trauma release exercises to reconnect with your body safely and gently. Trauma Recovery Discover practical methods for PTSD recovery and C-PTSD healing using pacing, self-awareness, and safe trauma work principles. Co-Regulation and Attachment Strengthen resilience, rebuild trust, and foster emotional balance through healthy connection and attachment repair. Mind-Body Integration Identify your fight, flight, and freeze responses, reduce emotional flashbacks, and reestablish harmony between mind and body. title: The 30-Day Anxiety Relief Journal for Women: Daily CBT Prompts to Calm Your Mind, Stop Ove
description: It's 2:47am. You're not asleep. You already knew you wouldn't be. Your brain is doing that thing again — replaying something someone said three days ago, rewriting your response, spiraling into every embarrassing thing you've ever said or done, then worrying about tomorrow, then worrying about worrying. And the worst part? You know it's irrational. You know. But knowing doesn't stop it. That's what nobody tells you about anxiety. It's not just the panic attacks. It's the exhausting invisible weight of it. The apologizing before you've even spoken. The reading every text four times before sending. The canceling plans because your body physically won't let you go. The years of saying "I'm okay" when you are anything but okay. You've tried to fix it. Breathing apps. Meditation. Therapy waitlists that stretch for months. You've Googled "how to stop overthinking" at midnight like the answer might finally be different this time. It wasn't. Here's what nobody told you: anxiety doesn't respond to willpower. It responds to being understood. That's exactly what this journal was built for. Not to silence your anxiety. Not to tell you to "think positive." But to sit with you in the middle of it — and slowly, gently, help you make sense of what's happening inside you. Every prompt is rooted in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) — the most clinically proven method for managing anxiety that exists. Not fluffy. Not vague. Real tools that actually work. Five minutes a day. That's all this asks of you. title: Anxiety and Overthinking: Easy Steps to Break Free from Negative Spirals and Triggers, Gai
description: You lie awake replaying a conversation word for word, certain you said the wrong thing. Tomorrow becomes a movie of worst-case scenarios. Even choosing dinner feels like one more decision you might ruin. And no matter how hard you think, you can't think your way into peace. This book contains practical steps that took me from years of anxiety and overthinking to steadier choices and calmer relationships. None of it requires a personality overhaul. It's built on small actions you can repeat on an ordinary Tuesday. The biggest shift? I stopped treating every anxious thought as a command and learned how to interrupt the cycle. Most adults were never taught the difference between useful problem-solving and the exhausting loop of overthinking. Once you can tell them apart, you can start choosing which one gets your attention. I tried methods, sought help, and faced setbacks before the small practices added up. Now I meet anxious moments with more skill and less panic. The CBT-based tools, grounding practices, and decision habits inside can help you do the same. Inside, you'll discover how to: Recognize your anxiety triggers with the Trigger Map exercise, identifying what sets off spirals at work, around money, in relationships, and everyday situations. Interrupt frightening "What if?" thoughts and turn them into calmer, more manageable next steps. Stop second-guessing every decision with practical strategies for overcoming analysis paralysis, embracing imperfect decisions, and moving forward with confidence. Challenge automatic negative thoughts with a step-by-step CBT Thought Record exercise that helps you examine and reframe unhelpful thinking patterns.
